terms.gloss: subjunctive; as a noun (modus understood), the subjunctive
evidence: Diom. p. 331 P.; Prisc. p. 820 P. (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The later grammarians’ term, from subjungere, to join on beneath: the mood of subordinate clauses. modus subjūnctīvus, the subjunctive mood; modō subjūnctīvō, in the subjunctive (Traupman 228). We have found no classical name for it.
Martianus Capella’s name, kept in some modern grammars.

phrases.latin: Dā dēclīnātiōnem ejusdem verbī āctīvī, tempore praesentī, modō subjūnctīvō, singulāriter.
phrases.english: Give the conjugation of the same active verb in the present subjunctive singular.

sources: Lewis & Short: subjunctivus · Lewis & Short: conjunctivus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 225, p. 228, p. 249.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
